gap: No result ChatGPT got puts prices on the three kinds of cabinet turntable side by side. As read at CSH Hardware on 2026-11-10, a complete Rev-A-Shelf two-shelf polymer kidney lazy susan for a 28" corner base cabinet, with a telescoping post for 26–31" interior height, costs $65.52. That is about 40% less than the $109.99 Dowell two-shelf kidney card ChatGPT showed. A bare 6" square bearing costs $3.27 and a shelf-top 11" OXO tray costs $16.99.
standout_why: Compared with kitchendesignnotes.com (18 products, Amazon links), 4stnotary.com/best-lazy-susan (7 products) and tidystow.com sizing guide. kitchendesignnotes and 4stnotary both say they quote no prices, and tidystow names no products. kitchendesignnotes gives load ratings (Dowell 40 lb/shelf with 13.5 lb per item; Rev-A-Shelf 24" kidney 50 lb/shelf) but no prices, and none of the three compares the corner-unit, shelf-tray and bearing options on cost. The cshardware.com collection pages in ChatGPT's results show single-store prices but do not compare them with the Dowell or OXO cards. That is why this scores 2 and not 3.
decides: If the shopper means a corner base cabinet with a hinged door, the cheapest complete fix is the Rev-A-Shelf Lazy Daisy polymer 2-tray kidney set at $63–66, not the $109.99 Dowell. The Dowell's steel build only pays off if the shopper wants chrome wire. For a cabinet that isn't a corner, an 11" tray (OXO, $16.99) needs at least a 13" opening under TidyStow's opening-minus-2" rule. For a DIY rotating shelf, a 6" bearing is about $3, so a $7.87 bearing is the cost of the brand, not a functional upgrade.
